title: Golf balls, a trash can and the Phillies’ wild fantasy football draft order
content:
PHILADELPHIA — On the Phillies’ off day Thursday, Trea Turner and Garrett Stubbs traversed Citizens Bank Park to find what Stubbs called the “best and (a) somewhat obscure” spot for their fantasy football draft. They looked in Ashburn Alley before ending up in the 300s. There they identified a handicapped seating area as the spot to send golf balls into a trash can set up in the outfield.

“Because everywhere else the railing would’ve ricocheted the golf ball, and somebody would have gotten hit in the teeth,” Stubbs said. “So (the grounds crew) took the railing off and then let us hit up there and then put the railing back on.”

About 4 1/2 hours before Friday’s game, the Phillies brought a golf club up and swung for the fences — or, really, the trash can. The best shots determined the order of their fantasy football team; Kyle Schwarber won, followed by Bryson Stott and Stubbs. Twelve players participated in the draft; some are sharing teams, like Stubbs and rookie Andrew Painter and relievers Chase Shugart and Brad Keller, so just one representative competed.

This is the time of year when many MLB teams decide their draft orders through decidedly ridiculous methods. Recently, the Toronto Blue Jays determined their draft order via a random drawing of support staffers who then competed to throw the fastest pitch. Kazuma Okamoto came away as the winner, per SportsNet.

And it isn’t cheap to join the Houston Astros’ draft, per Josh Hader’s recent appearance on “Foul Territory.”

“It’s $2,500,” Hader said. “It’s a good payout.”

In 2025, the Blue Jays parachuted army figures from the upper decks of Rogers Centre onto the field. In 2024, the Athletics threw baseballs off the Oakland Coliseum’s outfield behemoth, Mount Davis, to determine their draft order. The Phillies typically do a golf shot, but it’s been from home plate in previous years. The Los Angeles Dodgers have a draft set for their next road trip but have yet to figure out how they’ll determine the order. At least they have plenty of inspiration to draw from.

As for the most creative shot in the Phillies’ draft? Shugart holds that honor, hitting the State Farm sign next to Monty’s Angle, perhaps the biggest quirk of the outfield at Citizens Bank Park.

“He scalded it,” Stubbs said. “And went way over and just smoked the State Farm sign. And it actually ricocheted and made the shot a little bit better. Yeah, he had the 12th pick.”
